title: Professor Chaligny's lessons and big student band
summary: Uncle Clay took him to Old Man Chaligny, who taught at his St. Claude Street home for 25 cents and ran a large scholars' band that rehearsed at a hall.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well I got the set and my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons. And Old Man Chaloner was a teacher. He didn't only teach you. He made you experience of learning to play instruments. He would have a big band of all of his scholars. On Monday you'd go to lessons. On Wednesday all his scholars would be in the band together. So he taking my Uncle Clay to play the bass drum to give the youngsters ideas about a band being so big. So they brought me over and I would play the snare drum. But they had about 10 or 20 snare drums.

And he's such a good teacher if one musician would make a mistake, he could stop the band and pick him out. And he would talk about everybody. Because a blowing instrument, a drum, no care what it was. He would stop the whole band and tell them, hold on, just a minute. Unless you hit that beat again or make that roll again on the drum. Oh no, that's not perfect. Come again and he would hum the beats to you. La, la, la, la, to be sure that you make it perfect. Yeah. He's one of the greatest teachers I think they are.
By the way, where did he live? About where did he teach at his home or any special school? How was it?
He'd teach at his home and he would bring the band to St. Catron Hall.
That's right. That's where the band would be when he would have them all together. But he would teach at his home on St. Claude Street.
About where? What's that? Downtown here?
Yeah, St. Claude Street is, you know, around where the Japanese tea garden is in the era? Oh yeah, near St. That's right. That's right. That's right. That's where he lived. Around there.
You remember what he charged for lessons in those days?
Oh yeah, he was charging 25 cents.
